text:
Alyssa: kicking off Constella customer LoRA graft into the 1.2.0-serving branch. main goals: verify merge correctness, run int4/int3 quant smoke, and produce a tiny eval pack for product tests. pinging @Kim for the customer prompts.
Kim: got it — I have the CustConstella_promptset_v2 (120 examples) ready. will strip PII and export a 30-example quickpack for latency/quality. do you want balanced intents or bias toward transaction flows? :thinking_face:
Alyssa: prioritize transaction + edge cases (dates, amounts, locale variants). include a couple adversarial examples we saw in the ticket. keep pack <=30 to run fast in CI.
Julio: quick note — tokenizer diff after applying LoRA shows two changed token ids for currency symbol normalization. small but could shift logits. diff: ```- token 1623: "$" -> 36
+ token 1623: "\u0024" -> 36``` Might cause off-by-one detokenization for short templates.
Matt: thanks, Julio. that aligns with the customer report about dropped leading $ on small strings. Is this something we can patch in the merge or should we handle as a post-merge tokenizer remap?
Julio: we can remap at load time (fast patch) but better to record as model-vocab-mismatch in the manifest. I'll post a minimal patch.
Sana: for quant, I'm planning two runs on a single A100: int4 (nf4) fast path and int3 (experimental) with KCache disabled. baseline (fp16) -> int4 -> int3. I'll capture token-level perplexity and EM on the evalpack. any other metrics?
Kim: add exact-match on key fields (amount, currency, date), and a human-rated fluency flag (0/1). we can compute intent-f1 later but EM on those fields will catch regressions.
Alyssa: also capture generation latency P50/P95 for both streaming and non-streaming endpoints (30-token tail). we need cost delta estimate too.
DevBot: CI job triggered: run/eng-ml/constella-smoke/3487654321 (queued). logs will post here. :robot_face:
DevBot: run/eng-ml/constella-smoke/3487654321 -> started on a100-55gb. configs: 
```yaml
model: constella-lora-v2
base: small-sage-7b
quant: nf4-int4
kv_cache: enabled
batch: 4
max_tokens: 64
evalpack: constella-quick30.json
```
Matt: rough note — when you run int3, please set kv_cache: false per Sana above, we saw instability with int3+kv on other merges.
Sana: running int4 now, first pass results (30 examples): EM-fields: fp16 0.92 -> int4 0.90, fluency: fp16 0.98 -> int4 0.96, P95 latency fp16 210ms -> int4 160ms. cost per token estimate down ~38%. attaching short diff in outputs (two cases with currency rounding).
Kim: uploaded constella-quick30.json to the shared evals bucket (s3://redwood-evals/constella/quick30.json). I also added the gold labels for the fields. link: https://s3.redwood/constella/quick30.json
Alyssa: int4 looks promising. please kick int3 but tag it experimental. we need to verify hallucination rate (we care about inventing amounts).
Sana: int3 run started. preliminary looks noisier: EM-fields dropped to 0.86 on first 10 examples, but latency moved to 120ms P95. will run full 30 and post breakdown.
Julio: added token remap hook in model manifest, example config: ```json
{"token_remap": {"36": 1623}}
```
Matt: heads-up — if we keep remap, add a small postprocess check in the serving layer to ensure determinism across fp16/int4/int3. Otherwise customers see odd diffs.
Alyssa: agreed. action items: (1) Kim finalize quick30 with edge cases, (2) Julio push remap patch + manifest note, (3) Sana complete int3 run and post metrics, (4) Matt add postprocess assertion to serving smoke. I'll collect results for product review tomorrow.
Kim: done — quick30 updated w/3 adversarial currency/date examples.
Sana: int3 full done: EM-fields 0.85, fluency 0.92, hallucination (amount fabricated) flagged 3/30. raw logs: /runs/3487654321/int3/logs.txt.
DevBot: job run/eng-ml/constella-smoke/3487654321 -> completed (status: WARN). artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/constella/3487654321/artifacts.tar.gz
Alyssa: thanks team. I'll open a small PR bundling the remap + manifest + smoke ci step. If int3 regressions are unacceptable, we'll ship int4 + fallback policy to fp16 for those routes.
Matt: +1, and I'll add the serving assertion PR after Alyssa's.
Kim: can we add one synthetic test for amounts normalization to the regression suite? makes sense before canary.
Alyssa: yes — Kim add it and we'll gate the canary. closing thread once PRs are green. :white_check_mark:
